reason: Aborted plays brutal death metal/grindcore, and both lists live in that world. a_recs pairs one same-band track with strong scene neighbors: Cattle Decapitation, Hate Eternal, Unleashed and Origin all sit in the same brutal/technical death sphere. b_recs fits sonically too, but it is four more Aborted tracks plus Necrotted, and 'Interlude' is an instrumental interlude rather than a real song. a_recs offers comparable fit with actual discovery value.

Tour-Maubourg makes warm, jazzy deep house. Both lists sit in that world: a_recs leans on three more Tour-Maubourg tracks plus adjacent lo-fi/deep house from Boukas and dublon, all fitting but offering little beyond the artist himself. b_recs pairs one same-artist track with Felipe Gordon, Loure and Chaos in the CBD, all squarely in the same soulful deep-house scene, giving comparable fit with more range. Pierre Moritz I could not place. b_recs is the more useful 'more like this' list.

Graham Parker's late-80s singer-songwriter mode sits in the pub-rock/power-pop lineage. a_recs reaches across that scene: Nick Lowe and Marshall Crenshaw are natural companions, Frankie Miller shares the rootsy soul edge, only the Stranglers pick is off. b_recs is all Parker tracks that fit sonically but tell the listener nothing new, and the acoustic version is a weaker pick. a_recs is the more useful 'more like this' list.

I-Zax is a Thai pop-rock act; I know the artist's general style but not this specific track. In a_recs, Tattoo Colour's รักแรกพบ and the band's own ส่วนประกอบ fit the Thai pop-rock scene, NICECNX is adjacent Thai pop, but i-dle's 한(寒) is Korean pop with no stylistic link. b_recs stays within Thai guitar-pop/rock territory (Potato, 25 hours, plus I-Zax's own ปวดใจ) with no jarring outlier, so it is the safer, more coherent list despite several tracks I could not place.

Shirokuma is a Swedish screamo/post-rock band. a_recs is five more Shirokuma tracks — each fits sonically, but the list offers nothing a listener couldn't find by clicking the artist page. b_recs reaches across the screamo scene: Shizune, Usurp Synapse, Kidcrash and Cassus are all kindred chaotic/emotive hardcore acts, exactly the 'more like this' a listener wants. b wins on variety with equal or better fit.

Ahn Yeeun's 야화 is dark, dramatic art-pop steeped in traditional Korean sounds. a_recs captures that world well: 출항 is her own signature track, 심규선's 야래향 shares the eerie traditional-inflected mood, and 김예지's ALONE fits the dramatic vocal style. b_recs has one strong match (난파) but dilutes it with gentler folk/indie ballads (곽진언, 이한철, Heize) that lack the dark intensity, and an instrumental version of 출항 is a poor recommendation in itself.

陳建年's 海洋 is gentle Taiwanese indigenous folk. a_recs stays in that world: another 陳建年 track, indigenous folk peers 以莉.高露 and Suming, plus adjacent Taiwanese indie. b_recs has one strong same-artist fit (兰屿之恋) and reasonable folk-rock from 低苦艾, but 张学友's Cantopop ballad is a clear mismatch and 夜谭乐队 I cannot place. a_recs is the more coherent 'more like this' list.

早見優 is early-80s idol kayōkyoku. a_recs opens perfectly with 松田聖子 and a fitting 中森明菜 track (live version, still a real performance), but then drifts to 2000s J-rock/anisong (SNoW, God knows...) and 椎名林檎, which share little with the seed's sound. b_recs stays in the 80s idol world throughout — same-artist 早見優, 工藤静香, 荻野目洋子, 本田美奈子 — with only the 河合奈保子 karaoke track as a dud. b is the more coherent 'more like this' list.

The seed is a François de Roubaix soundtrack piece — 70s French film scoring with his signature melodic, lightly electronic touch. a_recs is four more de Roubaix cues, all fitting, but the Marie-Ève Janvier/Jean-François Breau pop duet is a total mismatch. b_recs pairs a de Roubaix theme with Cosma, Delerue, Jarre and Schäfer — the same French soundtrack/electronic world, and it opens up beyond the obvious. b wins on variety and no bad pick.

I do not know uju or this track well enough to characterize its sound, and most of the candidate artists (BehindtheMoon, Rainbow note, D2ear, Nahee, Kisnue, Life And Time) are Korean indie acts I cannot reliably place. Scoring would be guessing from titles and language, which the rules prohibit.

Tardor are a Catalan pop-rock band; I know the scene only broadly. a_recs leans on more Tardor tracks, which fit stylistically but make the list thin, plus Tremp from the same Catalan scene. b_recs reaches across Catalan/Spanish indie (Novembre Elèctric, Smoking Souls) but the Spanish-language picks (La Habitación Roja, Corazones Eléctricos) are only loosely adjacent. a_recs fits better despite the redundancy.

雪沉乐队 is a Chinese folk metal band, so same-band tracks (云中君, 迷僧) and fellow folk metal act 小雨/Mysterain fit best. 窒息, Yaksa and 唐朝 are Chinese metal but from thrash/classic scenes, only broadly adjacent. Two a_recs tracks I cannot place. b_recs offers a coherent spread of Chinese metal with folk leanings and no unplaceable picks, so it is the more useful list.

李明洋 is a Taiwanese Hokkien (台語) ballad singer, and a_recs is drawn entirely from that same scene — 江志豐, 袁小迪, 陳百潭, 黃文星 are all台語 pop singers with the same sentimental ballad style, plus another 李明洋 track. b_recs is Chinese-language hip-hop and rap (RAMBO GANG, 满舒克, etc.), a completely different genre and audience with no stylistic link to a台語 ballad.

I do not know 劉藴晴 Rachel or this track well enough to characterise its sound, and most of the candidate artists are equally unfamiliar to me, so I cannot judge fit honestly.

Air Raid is a Swedish NWOTHM band playing classic 80s-style heavy metal. a_recs is five more Air Raid tracks - stylistically on target but a thin result that opens nothing up. b_recs mixes one Air Raid track with Stallion, Morgul Blade, Sabïre and Enforcer, all squarely in the same traditional/speed metal revival scene; Enforcer is an especially close sonic match. b is the more useful 'more like this' list.

Kanade is a warm, melodic mid-2000s J-pop ballad. a_recs stays squarely in that world: Superfly's big emotional ballad, another Sukima Switch track, GReeeeN's Kiseki and Yuzu's Harukaze all share the heartfelt melodic J-pop character; Makihara is a generation earlier but stylistically close. b_recs is more scattered — Crystal Kay and Riria are plausible pop-ballad fits, Quruli and sleepy.ab lean indie/rock, and one track I cannot place. a is the more reliable 'more like this' list.

The query is the Spanish-language Ranma 1/2 opening theme, so the right neighborhood is Latin anime-theme covers. a_recs leans into that world: Mikami la Cazafantasmas and Mi Corazón Encantado (Dragon Ball GT) are the same kind of Spanish anime opening, and the Inheres track is another cover of the very same song. b_recs appears to mix in tracks by the unrelated 90s R&B group Jade plus a remix edit and a demo, which are poor fits; only the Blue Bird Naruto cover lands. a is the more coherent anime-theme list.

The Big Hash is a South African melodic hip-hop/R&B artist. b_recs stays in that world: another Big Hash track plus FLVME, Maraza, K.O and Fifi Cooper, all SA hip-hop peers with overlapping melodic trap sensibilities. a_recs is mostly obscure lo-fi/indie acts I can't place, and the two I can (Olivia Dean's neo-soul, Wye Oak's indie rock) sit outside the SA hip-hop scene. b is clearly the more useful 'more like this' list.

Blut aus Nord is dissonant atmospheric black metal, and a_recs is squarely in that world: another BaN track, Ruins of Beverast, Akhlys and Misþyrming all share the dark, experimental BM character, with Drudkh a slightly more folk-tinged but still close neighbor. b_recs is metalcore, rap-metal, big-beat electronica, a film score cue and a lofi beat — none share any stylistic ground with the seed.

Jubilee is a traditional Appalachian folk song from Jean Ritchie's dulcimer-and-voice repertoire. Every a_recs track is another Jean Ritchie traditional, so each fits sonically, but the list is just more of the same artist. b_recs matches the old-time/Appalachian folk revival world while reaching beyond: Cotten's fingerpicked guitar, the Kossoy Sisters' close-harmony balladry, Holcomb's high-lonesome Kentucky singing, and Henry Thomas's early rural recordings all sit naturally beside the seed. b wins on breadth without losing fit.

Krallice play dense, technical USBM. Every a_recs track is another Krallice song, so each fits perfectly on its own, but the list is just five more tracks by the same artist — thin as a recommendation. b_recs opens with the adjacent track from the same album, then reaches into genuinely adjacent scenes: Altar of Plagues' atmospheric black metal, Ante-Inferno's raw USBM, Mgła and Sinmara's orthodox black metal. All stylistically close while offering discovery. b wins on variety despite equal fit.

I do not know Chen Guo or this track well enough to characterize its sound — it could be indie folk, pop, or rock, and guessing would be unreliable. Per the rules, I return empty arrays rather than infer from the candidate lists.

Joyside are a Beijing garage-punk/indie rock band. a_recs stays in the Chinese indie rock scene: another Joyside track, The Big Wave's synth-rock, Muma's alt-rock, plus Zoo Nail House and Supermarket from adjacent indie/electronic corners — all plausible next plays. b_recs has one solid fit (Silly Girl) but the rest are obscure or unplaceable, and a Various Artists compilation slot is a poor recommendation. a is clearly the more useful list.

Iron Mind is an Australian hardcore band; I know the style but not this specific track. The Iron Mind tracks in both lists are safe same-band hardcore fits. The other candidates (False Reality, Wetwork, Secret World, Forewarned, Transforma) are too obscure for me to place honestly. b_recs is almost entirely Iron Mind, so it is reliably on-style, though it opens nothing beyond the band itself; a_recs is riskier but potentially more exploratory. Given the unknowns, b is the safer hand-off.
周云蓬是当代中国民谣/盲人民谣诗人，《九月》是海子诗改编的深沉民谣。b_recs几乎全是同一民谣场景：张玮玮（野孩子）、莫西子诗、陈粒、谢春花，加上周云蓬自己的《春歌》，气质高度吻合。a_recs里胡德夫是绝佳的民谣前辈，左小祖咒勉强相邻，但曹芙嘉是主流流行歌手，气质偏离，邻间少年无法判断。b整体更贴近种子曲的民谣世界。

SKRY sits in the French hardtek/tribe scene. b_recs is five more SKRY tracks - each fits the sound perfectly, but a listener who just played one SKRY track gains nothing new; it is a thin result. a_recs keeps one SKRY track and reaches across the same scene: Farfacid, Von Bikräv and Vortek's are all hardtek/frenchcore-adjacent acts that match the driving, loopy industrial energy. Fasotek I could not place. a_recs is the more useful 'more like this' list.

List b has a same-artist track and a decent Daniel Chan ballad, but two artists I cannot place and a Bibi Zhou track that is more modern pop. List a is the more reliable, coherent set.

Shin Yong Jae is a K-ballad/OST vocalist, so the right neighborhood is emotive Korean ballads. a_recs stays in that world: NELL's Kim Jong Wan OST ballad, an Ailee drama ballad, GB9's balladry, plus a same-artist OST cut. b_recs fits well too (Kim Na Young ballad, three more Shin Yong Jae songs) but EXO's Peter Pan is idol pop, off the ballad mood, and three same-artist tracks make it a thin result. a_recs matches the mood while reaching beyond the obvious.

List b is entirely artists I cannot place, with titles suggesting pop/rap rather than orchestral score, so none can be rated as a fit.

雨あがりの夜空に is a slow, soulful 1980 Japanese rock ballad. b_recs stays in the classic Japanese rock world: another RCサクセション track, SHEENA & THE ROKKETS from the same 70s-80s rock scene, and JUN SKY WALKER(S) adjacent 80s J-rock. a_recs drifts into 90s-2010s J-pop balladry (Mr.Children, 今井美樹, 新山詩織) with only サザン offering real adjacency. b is clearly the more scene-true list.

Summer Salt's breezy US surf-indie and 小松未歩's 90s J-pop are only surface-level connections. Several candidates I cannot place, so confidence is low; a edges b on the picks I can judge.

Roo'RA's '3!4!' is mid-90s Korean dance-pop with hip-hop flavor. a_recs hits exactly that scene: Turbo, Jinusean and Kim Sung Jae are the same era and sound, with YTC a plausible adjacent pick. b_recs is all Roo'Ra — '날개잃은 천사' fits perfectly and '착한사랑'/'연인' suit, but 'Jingle Bell' is a seasonal novelty and 'Hotel California' a cover, and five tracks by the same artist the listener just played opens nothing up.

CrowsAlive are a Japanese metalcore/post-hardcore band. a_recs stays in that world: another CrowsAlive track, Japanese scene-mates Story of Hope and BEFORE MY LIFE FAILS, and WEAKEND HEROES nearby. b_recs has one strong fit (Shrezzers' technical post-hardcore) and reasonable Western metalcore (I Prevail, Too Close to Touch), but mgk's pop-punk/rap is a poor match and ELLEGARDEN's punk is only adjacent. a_recs is the more coherent scene match.

I do not know Jurassic Shark or the track Maybe well enough to characterize its sound, and most of the candidate artists (ryster, Fake Tides, Junkie, The High Curbs) are equally unfamiliar, so I cannot judge fit honestly.

The seed is Joanna Wang's soft, jazzy acoustic take on Cat Stevens. a_recs is built of exactly that world: Mandarin indie-folk (Cheer Chen), her own catalog, and hushed acoustic covers by The Civil Wars and Daniela Andrade — all natural next plays. b_recs drifts into pop/R&B (Alaina Castillo), an Idolmaster character song, and two tracks I cannot place; only KaiL Baxley's folk leanings come close. a is clearly the more coherent list.

1TakeJay is LA street rap from the 1Take collective. a_recs is five 1TakeOcho tracks - same collective, same sound, essentially perfect fit, but it's a thin result: one artist, no discovery. b_recs spans the broader LA/West Coast rap scene (Capolow, $tupid Young, Rucci, Lil Pete) plus a 1TakeJay track, all stylistically adjacent. b offers comparable fit with real variety.

Genius of Time make warm, sample-driven deep house. I don't know Siwa or this track well enough to characterize its sound, and most of the candidates (JEONGMILLA, the other Siwa tracks) are equally unfamiliar to me. Scoring would be guessing from titles rather than musical knowledge.

Ceres is a Melbourne indie/emo band, and a_recs stays in that world: fellow Australian indie acts like Tiny Little Houses, Dear Seattle, Bec Stevens and Vera Blue share the scene and mood, plus another Ceres track. b_recs opens with three big-room EDM tracks (Kaaze, Maddix, Yellow Claw) that have no stylistic link at all; its two Ceres songs fit but can't rescue a list that is mostly wrong genre.

Brain Failure is a Beijing punk band, so the right neighborhood is the late-90s/2000s Chinese punk and pop-punk scene. b_recs lives entirely there: Underground Baby is first-wave Chinese punk, the Flowers tracks are same-scene pop-punk, and the Brain Failure track fits naturally. a_recs has two fitting Brain Failure songs but also a Glitch Mob electronic track, a Smashing Pumpkins alt-rock song, and a Mendelssohn orchestral scherzo — three tracks with no stylistic link to Chinese punk.
声音玩具是成都梦幻后朋/独立摇滚。两组推荐都在中国独立摇滚场景内：声音碎片、寸铁、木马、野外合作社都是气质相近的独立摇滚，棱镜偏流行摇滚稍远，贊詩和青山我不够熟悉。两组质量接近，b组的声音玩具同名曲、木马和野外合作社在阴郁诗性的气质上更贴近种子曲，略胜。

I do not know Eye of Horus or this track well enough to characterize its sound, and the candidate artists (Crimson Shadows, Protosequence, Brain Stem) are also unfamiliar to me. Scoring would be guesswork based on titles alone.

Jimmie Vaughan is a Texas blues guitarist, and b_recs is squarely in that world: Freddie King, Albert King, Howlin' Wolf, Joe Louis Walker, plus Vaughan himself. a_recs has some blues adjacency (Yardbirds, Clapton) but drifts into country (Ed Bruce) and tracks I can't place, making it much less reliable as a 'more like this' list.

Ha Hyun Sang makes emotive K-indie balladry, and both lists stay in that world. a_recs fits well but leans on three more Ha Hyun Sang tracks plus a live version, which is thin as a recommendation set. b_recs reaches into the adjacent scene — Hoppipolla (his own band), I'll, LUCY — all sharing the same wistful band-ballad sound, giving the listener somewhere new to go. b is the more useful list.

Sleepy John Estes is 1930s Tennessee country blues. I do not know Jonatan or the track 'Jesteś Ty' well enough to characterise its sound, and I cannot reliably place most of the candidate tracks either. Scoring would be guesswork based on names alone.

Kissing the Pink is mid-80s synth-pop/new wave. b_recs is squarely in that world: another KTP track plus ABC, Belouis Some, Classix Nouveaux and The Wild Swans, all era- and scene-adjacent. a_recs is mostly game-soundtrack and hardcore electronic material (USAO, Casey Edwards, Embark) plus a smooth-jazz standard, none of which connects to 80s new wave.

Arty Hill plays traditional honky-tonk. a_recs is five more Arty Hill tracks - stylistically on target but a thin result that opens nothing up. b_recs reaches into the same world: Billy Joe Shaver's outlaw songwriting and Bill Kirchen's twang fit honky-tonk well, while Pete Bernhard's folk-blues is a looser match. b offers comparable fit with real variety.

어른 is Sondia's melancholic ballad from the My Mister OST. a_recs is a coherent set of Korean emotional ballads and OST-adjacent singers: Jung Seung Hwan and Kim Feel are near-perfect fits, Baek Yerin and Heize sit comfortably in the same wistful K-ballad/R&B space. b_recs has good picks (IU's Dear Moon, also tied to My Mister; Sondia's own 첫사랑) but KirbLaGoop's Clean is an American rap track with no connection, and 015B is a 90s pop act with little stylistic link. a is far more consistent.

Cruel Force is German black/thrash/speed metal. b_recs is a perfect match: same band, plus Diabolic Night, Hellripper, Midnight and Desaster, all raw blackened thrash/speed from the same scene. a_recs is mostly off-target: Connan Mockasin and Yung Bae are unrelated genres entirely, Brand of Sacrifice is modern deathcore, and only In Flames and Insomnium share even the broad extreme-metal family, with a much more polished melodic sound.

VASSLINE is a Korean metalcore band; I know the artist's style but not this specific track. Slant is a Korean hardcore punk band - same national heavy scene and broadly adjacent aggression, but raw hardcore punk is a noticeable step away from VASSLINE's metallic, produced metalcore sound, so those tracks land as acceptable rather than strong fits. The b_recs are all VASSLINE's own songs, which by definition share the exact sonic character. Both lists are single-artist, so neither offers variety; b wins purely on closer fit.

Erev Shel Shoshanim is a classic Israeli folk ballad. a_recs leans into that world: Dror Yikra is a traditional Hebrew piyut, Yerushalayim Shel Zahav is the canonical Israeli folk classic, and La Rosa Enflorece is a Sephardic traditional piece — all strong fits. The last two a tracks I cannot place. The b_recs are all by 'Shir' with English titles that suggest a different act entirely, and I cannot verify their sound, so I scored them -1. a wins on its verifiable folk/traditional fits.

Yapoos is Jun Togawa's avant-garde new wave band. a_recs has two more Yapoos tracks plus Hikashu, a natural scene-mate; Hamada and Kiyoshiro are mainstream J-rock with little stylistic link. b_recs has two strong Jun Togawa picks (one a live version) but also enka (Ishikawa) and idol pop (Nakamori), which are far off. a_recs is more consistently in the right world.

EmptyORio is a Taiwanese indie rock act. a_recs draws from the same Taiwanese indie/punk scene: 當代電影大師, 巨大的轟鳴, 胖虎 and SHOOTUP all sit in that world, plus a same-artist track that fits by default. b_recs leans mainstream Mandopop (李千娜, 金城武, 萧闳仁) with only 打倒三明治 matching the indie scene, so most of its picks share language but not style.

熱寫生 is a Taiwanese indie rock band; I don't know the specific track but can place the scene. a_recs is four more songs by the same band — they fit sonically but open nothing up — plus 小老虎, a Beijing rapper with no real stylistic link. b_recs has one same-artist track and then stays inside the Taiwanese indie world (逃走鮑伯, 我是機車少女, Blueburn, 告五人), which is exactly the adjacent scene a listener would want. b is the more useful 'more like this' list.

Kit Chan's 喜欢你 is a gentle Singaporean Mandopop ballad. a_recs is a near-perfect match: Mavis Hee, Cass Phang, Joi Chua and Stefanie Sun are all Singaporean Mandopop ballad singers of the same era and scene, plus a fitting Kit Chan track. b_recs consists of obscure cover uploads and improvisational pieces by artists I cannot place, with no verifiable connection to the seed's style. a is clearly the useful list.

文千岁 is a Cantonese opera/classic Cantopop singer, and the seed is a traditional-style festive number. Both lists open with the same-artist 花开富贵, a strong fit. b_recs stays in the classic festive Cantonese lane with 刘凤屏's 今年胜旧年 and 张曼莉's 迎春花, matching the era and celebratory mood. a_recs drifts into 80s pop (谭咏麟) and an English-language Wynners cover, which sit much further from the seed's traditional sound.

The seed is WhoMadeWho's melodic house track remixed by RÜFÜS DU SOL - deep, emotive melodic techno. a_recs stays in that world: RÜFÜS themselves, Elderbrook, Adriatique's 'Miracle', and Hayden James all sit in melodic house/alt-electronic territory. b_recs has one great pick (RÜFÜS's Like an Animal) and Adriatique, but the two Armin van Buuren trance tracks are a noticeably different, more commercial EDM sound, and Spring Tide is unplaceable. a_recs is the more coherent fit.

Baaba Maal is a Senegalese singer blending traditional West African sounds with modern production. b_recs is squarely in that world: Youssou N'Dour is the closest possible peer, Oliver Mtukudzi and Rajery bring adjacent Zimbabwean and Malagasy roots sounds, Bongeziwe Mabandla fits the modern African folk vein, and another Baaba Maal track fits naturally. a_recs is a scatter of indie, folk-rock and jazz with no connection to the seed's scene or sound.

雷安娜's 舊夢不須記 is an early-80s Cantopop ballad. a_recs has strong fits (梅艷芳's 似是故人來, 陳麗斯's 問我, another 雷安娜 track) but 餓狼傳說 is an upbeat 90s dance-rock number that clashes badly with the mood. b_recs is steadier: 關正傑, 張學友 and 蔡國權 all sit in the same 80s Cantopop ballad world, with only the 徐小凤 live recording slightly off in era and format. b is the more coherent listen.

The query is a 1979 Taiwanese campus-folk classic. b_recs hits that scene directly: 童年 and 赤足走在田埂上 are core 校園民歌, 盼 is same-artist folk, and the 苏芮/費玉清 picks are at least era-adjacent Mandarin pop. a_recs wastes a slot on the query song itself, and 喀秋莎 (a Russian standard by a mainland harmony group) has no real stylistic link; only the two other 潘安邦 tracks genuinely fit. b is clearly the more useful list.

Darkest Horizon is a German melodic death metal band with symphonic touches. The a_recs are all more Darkest Horizon tracks — they fit by definition, but five songs by the same artist is a thin 'more like this' result. b_recs hits the exact scene: Mors Principium Est, The Halo Effect, Children of Bodom, Whispered and Engel are all melodic death metal with matching intensity and era, and the list actually opens up adjacent bands.

昴宿 Pleiades is a Taiwanese indie/post-rock act; I know the style only broadly. a_recs reaches into the adjacent East/Southeast Asian post-rock and shoegaze scene (Paint The Sky Red, TFAP, Themilo), which fits the instrumental-leaning sound. b_recs is almost entirely more tracks by the same artist — they fit, but the list offers nothing beyond what the listener already has, and 神宿 is unknown to me. a_recs is the more useful recommendation set.

Up & Down is a 2014 brassy, catchy girl-group dance track. a_recs' DDD is the same artist and era; Something, Bad Girl Good Girl, and What a Girl Wants are close early-2010s girl-group fits, though Apink's A L R I G H T skews sweeter. b_recs has Rollin' — nearly identical retro-brass summer vibe and revival sister — plus NoNoNo, Marionette, and Badkiz all in the same scene. b edges it on fresher discoveries and Rollin' being the standout fit.

The seed is Wawa's classic 1991 Mandopop ballad. b_recs sits squarely in that world: 陳淑樺's 夢醒時分 is the same era and bittersweet ballad style, 大雨 is another Wawa ballad, and 孟庭葦 and 鳳飛飛 are adjacent Taiwanese pop of the period; 木吉他's campus folk is a bit further out but still plausible. In a_recs I could only place 凤凰传奇's 刘三姐, an upbeat folk-pop number with no real link to the seed; the rest are artists I cannot place. b wins clearly.

Susumu Yokota's ambient/electronic work. In a_recs I can only place Kid Koala (turntablism, poor stylistic match) and 横田進, which is Yokota himself and fits well; the rest are unknown to me. b_recs is anchored by another Yokota track, plus Biosphere's glacial ambient, MEITEI's Japanese ambient electronics, and Mort Garson's warm synth pastoral — all squarely in the same contemplative electronic world. b is clearly the stronger, more coherent list.

The query is a Mandarin Buddhist devotional chant (Namo Amitabha) by Chen Shuang. a_recs stays entirely in that world: another chant by the same artist, Buddhist hymns and sutra recitations by Lin Manni, Fo Guang Shan and Imee Ooi-style devotional singers. b_recs has one perfect match (Yineng's Amitabha chanting) surrounded by Mandopop and electronic tracks with no devotional connection, which spoils the list.

Cavour is a Bolivian charango master of Andean folk. b_recs is all more Cavour — stylistically perfect fits but a thin result that opens nothing beyond the artist already playing. a_recs reaches across the same Andean/nueva canción world: Centellas and Los Calchakis are squarely in the Bolivian folk scene, another Cavour track fits directly, and Violeta Parra is adjacent Chilean folk. Only the Perri track is unplaceable. a_recs is the more useful 'more like this' list.

The seed is a soft, intimate bedroom-pop love song. In a_recs, the elijah woods track is the same gentle pop world, vaultboy sits squarely in that bedroom-pop scene, and Zack Tabudlo is adjacent romantic pop. In b_recs, Finding Hope's chill electronic pop is a plausible mood match, but the rest of both lists are artists I cannot place well enough to score. a_recs has more tracks I can stand behind as fitting.

香坂みゆき is an 80s idol-pop singer, so the right neighbourhood is 80s Japanese idol and light city pop. b_recs stays in that world: same-artist track, 芳本美代子 and 国分友里恵 are fellow 80s idols, 大滝詠一 and Youki Kudoh are adjacent city-pop territory. a_recs leans earlier and softer — チューリップ's 70s folk-rock and 来生たかお's balladry are only broadly adjacent, and two tracks I cannot place. b is the more coherent 80s idol set.

Dakis is a 70s Greek pop/laiko singer, and 'Tosa Kalokeria' is a nostalgic summer tune. In a_recs, Mila Mou and the Voskopoulos track sit in the right era and scene; Rena Morfi's retro swing and Malamas's entehno are off. In b_recs, the two extra Dakis tracks and the Hatzinasios classic fit the same Greek summer-song world, while Stereomatic C.E.O.'s indie electronica and the Tom Jones cover are weaker. b_recs is more consistently in the right style.

I'm proud is mid-90s Tetsuya Komuro-produced J-pop dance. b_recs is squarely in that world: globe is Komuro's own project, DEPARTURES is the same artist and producer, hitomi and SPEED are 90s Avex dance-pop, and GLAY is era-adjacent J-rock. a_recs is a scatter of unrelated Western folk and hyperpop with no connection to 90s J-pop.

邓典果DDG is a Chengdu-scene melodic trap rapper, so CDC-adjacent picks fit well. a_recs has solid scene matches (谢帝, AnsrJ, 那奇沃夫) but the live recording of 李毅杰Pissy is a weaker listen. b_recs leans into the same Chengdu/new-wave trap circle (Asen with thomeboydontkill, 法老) plus two more DDG tracks that fit the vibe, making it the more cohesive 'more like this' list despite one unknown slot.

Santiago Feliú is Cuban nueva trova, and both lists live in that world. a_recs is all Feliú brothers plus Noel Nicola — perfect fits but essentially more of the same artist, offering little discovery. b_recs reaches across the Latin American trova/cantautor scene: Milanés is the closest possible peer, Aute and Cabral fit the introspective singer-songwriter mode, and Chavela Vargas is a looser ranchera-adjacent match. b_recs is the more useful 'more like this' list.

The seed is Sibelius's solemn hymn (Finlandia chorale) — serene, devotional, often heard in choral form. a_recs leans into that sacred, contemplative choral world: Fauré's Sanctus and the King's Singers' Rakastava match the mood well, and the Sibelius Impromptu keeps the composer connection. b_recs stays with Sibelius but as virtuosic violin works — the dramatic concerto (listed twice in different recordings) is a poor mood match for a quiet hymn. a_recs fits the spirit better and avoids redundancy.

Hillbilly Rawhide is a Brazilian psychobilly/rockabilly outfit, so their own tracks in a_recs all fit sonically but the list is five songs by the same artist — nothing new for the listener. b_recs keeps one fitting Hillbilly Rawhide track and adds Matanza's rowdy country-punk (a strong scene match), plus Velhas Virgens and Confraria da Costa in the same Brazilian bar-rock orbit; Ludov's indie rock is the weak link. b_recs offers real discovery at similar fit.

BG8LOCC is a Taiwanese underground rapper; I know the scene but not this specific track. a_recs draws from the same Taiwanese hip-hop circle — Macdella, Multiverse and 阿跨面 are credible scene-adjacent picks, and the same-artist track likely fits. I cannot place EyeballRay or any of the b_recs artists (FTP, KANNA BUSH, 白鲨JAWS, Yosko, 三火flame) well enough to score them, so a_recs wins on the strength of its identifiable Taiwanese rap connections.

The seed is a Marathi Ganesh aarti by Ravindra Sathe, a devotional/film singer. Most candidates are obscure Marathi tracks I cannot place. Alisha Chinoy's Hindi pop is a clear misfit; Anand Shinde's devotional style and the Hindi bhajan in b are broadly adjacent; 'Woh Kisna Hai' is filmi devotional, a weaker link. a_recs leans on same-artist Marathi tracks which are likelier to sit in the same devotional/folk space, so it edges ahead despite the bad pop pick.

I don't know Seoul Music Ensemble or this track well enough to say what it sounds like, so I can't judge fit honestly. The b list looks like East Asian traditional/orchestral music and a looks like unrelated Western pop and electronic, but scoring on that basis would be guessing from names rather than knowledge.

Stompin' Bird is Japanese melodic punk (J-pop-punk/skate punk). a_recs draws from that exact Japanese melodic punk scene: Stompin' Bird themselves, Over Arm Throw, HOTSQUALL, locofrank - all tour-mate bands of the same 2000s melodic punk wave. b_recs has some fits (ザ50回転ズ garage-punk energy, STANCE PUNKS street punk, Hump Back's youthful punk), but the two Humbert Humbert folk-duo tracks are completely wrong genre, spoiling the list.

Itoko Toma makes gentle, minimalist Japanese ambient/modern-classical piano. List a has one same-artist track plus Haruka Nakamura and Lullatone, both in the right hushed ambient world, but two artists I cannot place. List b pairs two fitting Ólafur Arnalds piano pieces with two more Itoko Toma tracks; only Joakim Karud's lo-fi beat feels off. B is more reliably in the seed's quiet piano sphere.

LINION is a Taiwanese neo-soul/R&B artist. In a_recs, Room 335 is his own track in the same style, Osean is adjacent Taiwanese indie R&B, and 問題總部 is Taiwanese indie — reasonable scene fits; Karen Mok and Eric Chou are mainstream Mandopop, only loosely related. In b_recs, 想不起你的名字 is another LINION track and fits, but the other four are obscure mainland ballad singers I cannot place. a_recs is the more grounded, scene-coherent list.

Stilz sits in the dark synthwave/retrowave scene, and both lists draw entirely from that world: VHS Dreams, NightStop, Absolute Valentine, Timecop1983 on one side; Fury Weekend, PYLOT, Jasper Byrne, Perturbator, Mitch Murder on the other. Every pick is a plausible next track for a synthwave listener, with Perturbator and Absolute Valentine leaning darker, Timecop1983 and Mitch Murder dreamier. Neither list has a dud or a redundancy problem, so there's nothing to separate them.

I do not know the track 'Deep Breath' or the artist Yoga Motion well enough to characterize its sound, and the candidate tracks are equally obscure yoga/ambient releases I cannot place. Scoring would be guessing from titles rather than knowledge of the music.

The seed is an acoustic cover of the Lewis Capaldi ballad, so fit means stripped-down acoustic pop covers. b_recs is built exactly from that world: another Plamina acoustic cover, Grace George's acoustic Heaven, and similar acoustic cover projects (Clementine Duo, Daniel Robinson) — modest individually but stylistically on target. a_recs drifts to contemporary R&B (Tinashe, GIVĒON) and jazz (Carmen Cuesta), which share little with an acoustic pop cover, and two slots I couldn't place.

The seed is German shanty-choir music. Both lists stay in that world: a_recs mixes same-choir tracks with other shanty choirs, plus Santiano (related but poppier) and Curd Jürgens (Hamburg song, not a shanty). b_recs leans heavily on the same choir plus another shanty choir's medley; Klaus Kohrs I cannot place. a_recs offers more variety across the scene while b_recs is mostly more of the same artist, so a is the more useful list despite b's strong fits.

Shennumbanine is Dutch drill/rap. Skengdo fits the drill sound well; Leafs, Mensa, Qlas & Blacka and MocroManiac are all adjacent Dutch street-rap acts, roughly comparable fits. The same-artist tracks (First Day Out, Gorilla Rap, Cowboy Bop) sit in the same style. Two tracks I cannot place. Lists are closely matched; b has slightly more scene variety while a leans on the seed artist twice, but both are thin in different ways — call it a tie.

Jaguar are a NWOBHM band and 'Axe Crazy' is raw early-80s British metal. a_recs is four more Jaguar tracks — they fit sonically but tell the listener nothing new — plus 'One of Us' by Jagúar, a different (Icelandic funk) act with no stylistic link. b_recs mixes one Jaguar track with Hollow Ground, Girlschool, Ostrogoth and Tysondog, all squarely in the same NWOBHM scene and era. b is both well-fitting and genuinely exploratory.

Huun-Huur-Tu are Tuvan throat singers; both lists fit that world. b_recs is four more Huun-Huur-Tu tracks - all excellent fits but offering nothing beyond the artist already playing - plus one Chinese track I cannot place. a_recs spans the Tuvan/Mongolian scene: Yat-Kha, Alash, Egschiglen, Altai Khangai all share the overtone-singing and steppe-folk character while opening up related artists, making it the more useful 'more like this' list.

Kieran Kane is spare, bluesy Dead Reckoning-scene Americana. a_recs stays close: Kevin Welch is the same label scene, the Kane tracks fit naturally, and Rayna Gellert's old-time fiddle is adjacent if rootsier. b_recs has a fitting Kane track and Gurf Morlix, but Neal Casal, Old 97's and Lucero lean toward louder alt-country/roots-rock, a step off Kane's quiet groove. a_recs is more cohesive despite leaning on the same artist.

250 makes sleek Korean electronic/house-tinged productions. a_recs wanders globally: ANII's melodic techno and Bellaire's French house are loosely adjacent, Parov Stelar's electro swing is a stretch, and Bad Omens' metalcore is a flat miss; only the other 250 track really lands. b_recs stays in the Korean electronic/indie scene (Clazziquai, XXX, O.O.O), which matches the seed's world far better, though it wastes a slot re-recommending the query song itself. b is the more useful list despite that.

Niaz Nawab is a Persian pop singer with a melodic, romantic style. a_recs leans on his own catalog (Kahroba, Bâdeh), which fits directly, plus Erwin Khachikian's Persian pop; but دریا is just the query song itself in Persian script, a wasted slot. b_recs offers adjacent Iranian acts (Pallett, Namjoo, Radio Tehran) that are more alternative/experimental than Nawab's classic pop, so fit is looser despite more variety. a wins on closer stylistic match.

脏手指 is a Shanghai lo-fi garage-punk band. b_recs stays in the Chinese indie/punk world: another Dirty Fingers track, noise-punk 假假條, garage-rock Joyside, and 回春丹, with 郭顶 as a softer but adjacent indie pick. a_recs mixes Cantopop (林子祥), a Chinese rapper (满舒克) and several tracks I cannot place, none of which connects to the seed's scrappy punk sound. b is clearly the more useful list.

四分衛 is a Taiwanese alt-rock band, and a_recs stays squarely in that world: Mary See the Future, Hello Nico and 甜約翰 are all Taiwanese indie-rock peers with overlapping moody guitar textures, and 脫拉庫 is an older Taiwan rock act. b_recs drifts into Mandarin pop (李千娜, 曾轶可) with little stylistic link, though THE 尺口MP, 顶楼的马戏团 and the 四分衛 track itself are reasonable rock fits. a_recs is the more coherent 'more like this' list.

Marc Robine sings literary, folk-tinged French chanson with anarchist and traditional leanings. a_recs sits squarely in that world: Vian's anti-war classic, Marchais's anarchist repertoire, Ogeret's chanson réaliste, Yacoub's folk revival, plus another Robine track. b_recs is 60s French pop and yé-yé (Hills, Christophe, Lai's film theme) plus modern indie pop — same language, wrong scene and mood entirely.

Bella is melodic Norwegian deep house. a_recs is entirely Finnebassen's own catalogue and remixes - every track fits sonically, but it offers nothing a listener doesn't already have. b_recs keeps the same early-2010s deep house world (Miguel Campbell, Karmon, Teenage Mutants) while reaching beyond one artist, making it the more useful 'more like this' list.

The seed is Kenji Kawai's Ghost in the Shell choral piece reworked as a Steve Aoki EDM remix, so it sits between cinematic Japanese music and festival EDM. In a_recs only Dimitri Vegas's big-room track is placeable and it matches the remix's EDM energy; the rest are too obscure to judge. b_recs leans into the Japanese doujin/Touhou electronic scene (EastNewSound, Senya, Risa Yuzuki), which fits the Japanese electronic character but not the EDM punch; Tama's 90s J-pop is a weak link. b is more coherent and placeable overall.

Aloha is mid-2010s French chill/tropical electronic. b_recs is essentially that exact scene: Tez Cadey, Petit Biscuit, Feder and Montmartre are all French touch chill-house peers, plus a same-artist Møme track that fits naturally. a_recs drifts elsewhere — Cannons' hazy cover and Rhye's downtempo R&B are only loosely adjacent, while Ash Code's darkwave and Camera Obscura's twee indie pop have no real connection to the seed's sound.

The Look of Love is lush early-80s UK sophisti-pop/new wave. a_recs is squarely in that world: another ABC hit, plus Frankie Goes to Hollywood, Pet Shop Boys, Kajagoogoo and Nik Kershaw — all era- and scene-adjacent British pop. b_recs is modern rap/R&B (Denzel Curry, King Von, Kelis) with no stylistic link to the seed; only Kelis's polished pop-R&B has even a faint groove connection.

白虹 is a 1940s Shanghai shidaiqu singer, so the gold standard here is other shidaiqu vocalists. Both lists deliver: a_recs has 龔秋霞 and 周璇 plus another 白虹 track, but drags with 謝雷's later Taiwanese pop and 田震's 90s rock ballad. b_recs pairs 周璇 and 吳鶯音 (both excellent era fits) with two more 白虹 tracks; 胡德夫's 70s folk is off, and 麻雀与小孩 is a children's piece, weaker stylistically. b's core fits are stronger and its misses no worse.
I do not know Fırat Durak or the track Glances well enough to say what it sounds like, and the candidate artists are obscure to me as well. Scoring would be guessing from names alone.

The seed is Armenian classical solo piano by Mikael Ayrapetyan. a_recs is entirely unrelated pop, rap and R&B with no stylistic connection whatsoever. b_recs stays in the classical piano world: two more Ayrapetyan pieces in the same intimate miniature vein, plus Buniatishvili's Romantic and Scarlatti repertoire, which shares the solo-piano character even if the mood differs. Clear win for b.

So What is mid-2000s Southern hip-hop (Field Mob with Ciara). b_recs lives in exactly that world: Lil' Flip and Chingy are same-era Southern rap, Ciara is literally the track's guest vocalist, Kelly Rowland is adjacent mid-2000s R&B; only Salt-N-Pepa is off-era. a_recs is mostly obscure tracks I can't place, and the two I can (Men I Trust's dream-pop, Melanie Martinez's alt-pop) share nothing with the seed's sound.

SADOG sits in the Taiwanese indie/emo-leaning rock scene. Both lists draw from that world: a_recs has 當代電影大師 and 午夜乒乓, solid Taiwanese indie fits, plus mainland indie acts that are broadly adjacent. b_recs pairs a same-artist track with SHOOTUP's emo energy and other Taiwanese indie acts (魚條, EmptyORio, hue), which feels marginally closer to SADOG's specific sound. I don't know most individual tracks, so scores are scene-level estimates and confidence is low.

李佳隆 is a melodic Chinese hip-hop artist, and a_recs stays squarely in that scene: his own 路灯, plus GALI, 艾热, 黄旭 and Juice Boy, all Chinese-language rap with adjacent melodic/emotional rap sensibilities. b_recs is mostly artists I cannot place (plus a Japanese track), so I can't verify any fit there. a_recs is the clearly safer, scene-consistent list.

7SENSES is SNH48's dance-focused subunit, so the closest scene is the 48-group family. b_recs draws heavily from that world: SNH48 songs and members (including 7SENSES' own Kiki Xu and Wu Zhehan) plus sister group BEJ48, all sharing the same C-pop idol sound; the live cut of 夜蝶 loses a little. a_recs has one perfect same-group track and an SNH48 song, but then drifts to broader C-pop soloists and a boy group with a different character. b is the more coherent 'more like this' list.

Vincy Chan is a Hong Kong Cantopop ballad singer, and a_recs stays squarely in that world: Sherman Chung, Sammi Cheng, Mag Lam and Vincy herself all deliver the same polished HK pop-ballad style; the Leo Ku live cut is a slight step down. b_recs is patchier — Jade Kwan fits well and Freya Lim is a reasonable Mandopop neighbour, but the two Steven Ma TVB-theme tracks are only loosely connected and one pick is unplaceable. a_recs is the more consistent list.

Yukadan (憂歌団) is a long-running Japanese blues band, and a_recs is five more of their own tracks, including their GeGeGe no Kitaro material — same voice, same bluesy feel, so each fits well even if the list is redundant and opens nothing up. b_recs has one strong same-artist blues pick (シカゴ・バウンド), but Folk Crusaders is 60s folk rather than blues, BEGIN is Okinawan pop, and two slots I cannot place. a wins on reliable fit despite the single-artist monotony.

Lianie May is an Afrikaans pop singer; I know the style but not these specific tracks. a_recs is five more Lianie May songs - they fit by definition but offer nothing beyond the artist the listener just played. b_recs keeps one Lianie May track and adds Brendan Peyper, Jo Black, Jay and 4Werke, all within the same contemporary Afrikaans pop scene, so it matches the sound while actually opening up the genre. b is the more useful list.

Let's Active is early-80s jangle pop from Mitch Easter's Athens/Winston-Salem scene. a_recs nails it: The Records' power pop, another Let's Active track, Robyn Hitchcock's guitar psych-pop, Love Tractor's Athens jangle, and Sloan's power pop all sit in the same guitar-pop lineage. b_recs is a scatter of 80s synth-pop, hi-NRG, and pub-folk with no stylistic link to jangly college rock.

Sinmara plays dissonant Icelandic black metal. Every a_recs track is another Sinmara song, so each fits perfectly, but the list is just more of the same artist. b_recs reaches across the exact scene: Almyrkvi, Svartidaudi and Skáphe are fellow Icelandic dissonant/atmospheric black metal acts, and Mgła is the closest Polish counterpart in hypnotic, mid-tempo black metal. b_recs matches the fit while actually opening up the scene.

Catie Curtis is a folk/Americana singer-songwriter. a_recs draws from exactly her scene: Deb Talan (The Weepies), Antje Duvekot, Gretchen Peters and the Secret Sisters all share the acoustic folk/Americana character. b_recs is five more Catie Curtis tracks - they fit sonically, but a listener who just played one of her songs gains nothing new from a list that is entirely the same artist.

Suyano makes Revealed-style big room/electro house. In a_recs, Shockwave is the same artist's own big room work, JAGGS and Kill The Buzz are core Revealed-scene acts, and Sultan + Shepard sit adjacent in festival progressive. In b_recs, Manse and Arston fit the melodic big room/progressive space well, but WildVibes, SSR and Deagon I cannot place confidently. a_recs has more verifiable scene fit, so it edges the verdict despite several unknowns on both sides.

Garion is Korean underground boom-bap hip hop. Both lists mostly pull from the Korean hip-hop scene: Junoflo, Primary and Infinite Flow fit well in a_recs, but Jaurim is a rock band with no stylistic link and Type-RUKU I cannot place. b_recs has Garion's own Post Mortem plus YDG and ONESUN, all squarely in the same scene; the PSY intro and Outsider are weaker but still hip-hop adjacent. b_recs is the more consistent list.

Effie is part of the Korean underground hyperpop/digicore scene. a_recs leans on Effie's own tracks, which should match the glitchy, pitched-vocal sound closely, though I can't place every title. b_recs draws from adjacent Korean underground artists (YUZION, kegøn, Cloudybay, ksmartboi) — same broad scene but several lean more toward trap/rage than Effie's hyperpop character. a_recs is the safer fit despite being same-artist heavy; several tracks on both sides I couldn't verify.

Sandee Chan is Taiwanese alternative/indie pop with a literate, offbeat edge. List a has one same-artist track and a fitting 自然卷 acoustic cut, but 李霄云 is only loosely adjacent and the KeyNG rap track is a clear miss. List b stays in the right Mandopop-alternative world: 楊乃文 is an excellent scene match, Yo Lee fits the indie-folk side, and while A-Lin and 梁文音 lean mainstream ballad, nothing is badly wrong. b is the more coherent list.

Labios rotos is a dreamy Mexican alt-rock ballad. a_recs stays in that world: Enjambre, Zoé themselves, and León Larregui's solo work are near-perfect scene matches, with La Castañeda and San Pascualito Rey darker but still Mexican rock adjacent. b_recs opens with two unrelated EDM/techno tracks, then a live cover, then two Cyrillic-titled tracks I cannot verify as real Zoé songs. a_recs is clearly the useful list.

小半 is 陈粒's hushed indie folk-pop. In a_recs, 芳草地 is the same artist's own folk material and 宋冬野's 斑马,斑马 sits in the same Chinese folk scene; the other three I cannot place. In b_recs, 郑润泽's moody pop-R&B is broadly adjacent, but 人間椅子 is a Japanese heavy psych-metal band — a clear misfire — and two slots are unknown to me. a_recs has the confirmed folk-scene fits and no obvious wrong pick.
I do not know Pay4n or this track, and most of the candidate artists (Teki, WickedRuna, IMIS!, 22december, KIDR) are also unfamiliar, so I cannot judge fit honestly.

Lujiachi is a Taiwanese experimental electronic producer; I know the scene but not this specific track. a_recs is four more Lujiachi tracks plus a remix he did of Dirty K - all presumably in the same sonic world, but it's a thin, self-referential list. b_recs reaches into the adjacent Taiwanese experimental scene (Meuko! Meuko!, Scintii) which fits well, but Lifeformed's game-soundtrack ambience and Lily Chou-Chou Lied's indie band sound are off, and Triodust I can't place. a wins on consistency despite redundancy.

The Hertz are a Hong Kong indie rock band with a dreamy, Cantonese indie-pop sound. a_recs stays in the broader Chinese/HK indie world: Schoolgirl Byebye and WHIZZ are close scene neighbours, Everfor and Yoyo Sham are softer but adjacent. b_recs has three more The Hertz tracks that fit sonically but open nothing up, plus a patriotic conservatory choir piece that is completely out of place and a Chinese indie track with only a surface link. a is the more useful and coherent list.

a_recs is five more Dead Kennedys tracks from the same early-80s hardcore world — all fit, but a listener who just played one DK song hardly needs five more served back. b_recs keeps Police Truck plus adjacent SoCal/DC hardcore: Agent Orange's surf-punk, Minor Threat's straight-edge blast, Geza X's LA punk satire. The Dickies' Sound of Silence cover is punk but novelty-leaning. b offers the same scene with real breadth.

Cryfemal is Spanish raw black metal. a_recs mixes a same-artist track with adjacent raw/depressive black metal (Dodsferd, Xasthur, Trhä) — all plausible fits, though Trhä's cosmic ambient-black style is a stretch and Despondent Moon I can't place. b_recs is five more Cryfemal tracks: each fits perfectly, but a listener who just played one Cryfemal song gains nothing new from a list that is only more of the same artist. a_recs offers real discovery within the right scene.

ダウト is a visual kei band, and a_recs stays in that world: another ダウト track, vistlip, メガマソ and DIAURA are all VK peers, with MIYAVI a looser but plausible adjacency. b_recs opens well with D and DaizyStripper, both genuine VK fits, but then collapses into 大堀めしべ's novelty enka and two AKB48-family idol pop tracks, which share nothing with the seed's sound or scene.

品冠's 我以為 is a gentle Mandopop heartbreak ballad from the 無印良品 lineage. a_recs stays squarely in that world: 梁文音, 林凡, 林宇中 and Aska Yang all deliver the same soft, melancholic Mandopop balladry, and 最想念的季節 is 品冠 himself. b_recs has two excellent 光良 picks (same scene, same voice family) but three tracks by artists I cannot place, making the list unreliable. a is the safer, consistently fitting set.

The seed is a well-known Marathi Vitthal bhajan by Shubhangi Joshi. Most candidates are obscure Marathi/Hindi bhakti tracks I cannot place, so I scored only what I know: Choti Choti Gaiyya is a Hindi Krishna bhajan (adjacent but different language/tradition), Avaghe Garaje Pandharpur is a classic Marathi abhang and a strong fit, Jaanta Raja is a Marathi Vitthal devotional in the same world, and the Hanuman aarti is broadly devotional but Hindi. b_recs contains the closest stylistic matches to the seed's abhang tradition.

Karaindrou's world is melancholic Greek film music with accordion and strings. a_recs reaches across that scene: Reboutsika is a near-perfect match, Farjad's mournful violin and Preisner's contemplative score fit well, Gokcin's piano is looser. b_recs has three more Karaindrou tracks that fit perfectly but tell the listener nothing new, plus a decent Badalamenti pick and a weaker Woodkid one. a_recs offers the richer 'more like this' result.

I do not know the artist lang or the track IHATOV well enough to describe its sound, so I cannot judge fit. The a-list candidates (くだらない1日, killie, moreru, Ling tosite sigure) suggest a Japanese indie/emo/screamo neighbourhood, and b_recs is mostly same-artist tracks plus a Lang Elliott nature recording, but without knowing the seed's style any score would be a guess.

Kärntner Viergesang is a Carinthian dialect folk vocal group; I know the style but not the individual tracks, so same-artist picks are scored as good fits on style. a_recs is entirely the same group — likely fitting but a thin result that opens nothing up. b_recs offers one same-artist track plus Der Montanara Chor, a German folk choir in the same broad alpine choral-folk family, giving variety at a slight fit cost. b is the more useful list.

Yamanaka is a contemporary Japanese jazz pianist; a_recs stays entirely in the Japanese jazz/fusion world (Terai, Casiopea, Honda, Matsumoto) and every track is a plausible next listen. b_recs has three good fits (Katayama and two Yamanaka tracks) but the Alchemist megamix is a sprawling beat-tape collage with no relation to acoustic jazz piano, and Yamashita's city pop is only a surface connection. a_recs is the more consistent list.

Selvageria is Brazilian thrash metal. b_recs is five more Selvageria tracks — each fits the raw thrash style, but the list offers nothing a listener doesn't already have. a_recs reaches into the adjacent Brazilian extreme scene (Desalmado's grind, Impurity's death metal) which suits the seed's aggression, though the MegaDriver game-soundtrack cover is a poor fit and Trovao is unknown to me. a_recs is the more useful 'more like this' list.

Kawa plays Yunnan roots reggae with ethnic-folk elements. In a_recs, the Kawa track fits perfectly and Skaraoke's ska is reggae-adjacent, but the two Xie Tianxiao tracks are Beijing grunge-rock — same broad Chinese indie world, different sound. In b_recs, the Kawa track fits, Hanggai's drinking song shares the folk-roots drinking-song spirit, and Li Naluo is a fellow Yunnan ethnic artist. b_recs leans closer to the Yunnan folk-roots scene overall, though several tracks on both sides are obscure to me.

Heart Attack is 2013 dance-pop with a big belted chorus. b_recs stays in that world: another Demi power-pop single, peak Taylor Swift pop, Avril's pop-punk energy, Becky G's bubblegum pop, and Nick Jonas's adjacent pop-R&B. a_recs is mostly unplaceable obscurities; The Cab's Endlessly is at least the right pop-rock ballpark, but the rest I cannot verify as fitting at all.

Totenwache plays raw German black metal in the Eisenwald-adjacent underground. a_recs draws from exactly that circle: Mavorim and Non Est Deus are close sonic kin, Runenwacht fits the same raw German BM niche, and Dark Fortress is German black metal though more polished and melodic. b_recs is five more Totenwache tracks - each fits perfectly on sound, but a listener who just played one Totenwache song gains nothing new from a list that is only the same artist. a_recs matches the scene while opening it up.

譚炳文 represents classic Cantonese oldies/時代曲. b_recs opens with 鄭錦昌's 新禪院鐘聲, a near-perfect match in era and Cantonese oldie style, and Frances Yip fits the 70s HK scene. a_recs leans on Cantonese opera (任劍輝), which is adjacent but a different idiom, plus 蔡琴 (Mandarin) and 90s Jacky Cheung. Both lists have weak modern picks, but b's strongest matches are closer to the seed's world.
